name: PEDIATRIC Rhabdomyosarcoma: VAC (vinCRIStine + Actinomycin-D/Dactinomycin + Cyclophosphamide), with optional alternating VI (vinCRIStine + Irinotecan)
histology: embryonal (typically FOXO1 fusion-negative) or alveolar (typically FOXO1 fusion-positive) rhabdomyosarcoma; FOXO1 fusion status is a stronger outcome predictor than histologic subtype
stage: high-risk (by Stage, Clinical Group, age, and FOXO1 fusion status)

biomarkers.FOXO1_fusion: gene-fusion status (PAX3::FOXO1 or PAX7::FOXO1) drives risk stratification; fusion-positive disease has unfavorable outcome and intensifies therapy/nodal management
biomarkers.note: PEDIATRIC. FOXO1 (PAX3::FOXO1 or PAX7::FOXO1) fusion status is the key prognostic molecular marker and is a stronger predictor than histology; alveolar RMS is typically fusion-positive and embryonal RMS typically fusion-negative. FISH for FOXO1 is sufficient. Risk group (low/intermediate/high) is assigned from Stage, Clinical Group, age, and FOXO1 fusion status. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma (Rhabdomyosarcoma) v1.2026, Molecular Alterations Table 1 (lines 1133 to 1157), fusion-status prognostic significance (lines 1029 to 1035, 1063 to 1066), FISH sufficiency (line 1109), and risk-group assignment (lines 600 to 621). No endorsement implied.

treatmentSetting: multimodal curative-intent systemic therapy (with surgery and radiation for local control), risk-adapted
lineOfTherapy: first-line systemic therapy for newly diagnosed rhabdomyosarcoma (risk-adapted)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: newly diagnosed rhabdomyosarcoma assigned to a risk group (low/intermediate/high) by Stage, Clinical Group, age, and FOXO1 fusion status
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v1.2026, Risk-group assignment (lines 600 to 621); Principles of Systemic Therapy (PRMS-G, lines 1692 to 1767)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: nodal sampling recommended for FOXO1 fusion-negative RMS with N1/metastatic disease and for all fusion-positive RMS
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma

drugs.name: vinCRIStine

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma
provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (PRMS-G): VAC (Vincristine/Dactinomycin/Cyclophosphamide) per COG ARST0331/ARST0531/D9803/ARST2031 (lines 1698, 1723 to 1755)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC. vinCRIStine is the V of VAC (and of the optional alternating VI). The source names the regimen and cites the COG protocols but does NOT print per-dose milligram values, so basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are the literal VERIFY (never invented). ISMP tall-man (vinCRIStine); 2 mg per-dose cap retained as a standard safety guard.

drugs.name: Actinomycin-D (Dactinomycin)

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma
provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (PRMS-G): VAC per COG ARST0531/D9803/ARST2031 (lines 1698, 1723 to 1755); dactinomycin held during RT (footnote b, line 1705)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC. Actinomycin-D (dactinomycin) is the A of VAC. Per-dose milligram value is NOT printed, so basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are VERIFY. Dactinomycin should be held during overlapping radiation (footnote b, cycle 6/week 16, line 1705).

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma
provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (PRMS-G): VAC backbone cyclophosphamide CUMULATIVE dose 16.8 g/m2 per ARST0531 (intermediate-risk, line 1725; high-risk ARST2031, line 1753); 30.8 g/m2 per D9803 Arm A (lines 1726, 1754); 8.4 g/m2 when VAC alternates with VI (lines 1727, 1755)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC. Cyclophosphamide is the C of VAC. The source prints CUMULATIVE doses by protocol (16.8 g/m2 VAC per ARST0531/ARST2031; 30.8 g/m2 per D9803 Arm A; 8.4 g/m2 when alternating with VI) but NOT the per-dose milligram value, so basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are VERIFY. Higher cumulative cyclophosphamide increases prolonged neutropenia/sepsis risk and gonadotoxicity; consider lower/intermediate cumulative dose (8.4 to 16.8 g/m2) in poor-performance patients with high Oberlin risk factors (footnote d, lines 1764 to 1767). Mesna may be used as clinically indicated (footnote a, line 1704).

drugs.name: Irinotecan (optional, alternating VI)

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma
provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (PRMS-G): VAC alternating with VI (Vincristine/Irinotecan) per COG ARST0531/ARST1431 (lines 1727 to 1728, 1755)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC OPTIONAL. Irinotecan is the I of the alternating VI (vinCRIStine/Irinotecan) block used with a VAC backbone in intermediate- and high-risk COG regimens (ARST0531/ARST1431). Per-dose milligram value is NOT printed, so basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are VERIFY. Include only when the VAC-alternating-VI schedule is selected.

premedications.name: Mesna
premedications.notes: may be used with cyclophosphamide as clinically indicated (footnote a, line 1704)

supportiveCare: Regimen family by risk group: low-risk = VAC per ARST0331 (or VA per D9602); very-low-risk may use VA alone for 22 weeks (EpSSG RMS 2005) (lines 1696 to 1699). Intermediate/high-risk = VAC backbone (ARST0531 cumulative cyclophosphamide 16.8 g/m2; D9803 Arm A 30.8 g/m2) or VAC alternating with VI (8.4 g/m2), plus optional oral cyclophosphamide/vinorelbine maintenance (ARST1431/ARST2031) (lines 1720 to 1767).

cycleLengthDays and cycles are VERIFY: the source names the COG protocols and prints cumulative cyclophosphamide but not a per-cycle length or cycle count; these must be resolved from a cited COG dosing source before activation.

cyclophosphamide: higher cumulative dose increases prolonged neutropenia/sepsis and gonadotoxicity; consider dose de-intensification (8.4 to 16.8 g/m2) with poor performance and high Oberlin risk factors; mesna as indicated.

multimodal: systemic therapy is integrated with surgery and radiation for local control; radiation begins around week 13 for most patients (dactinomycin held during overlapping RT) (footnote b, line 1705).
G-CSF: VAC is myelosuppressive; add per febrile-neutropenia risk.

monitoring: CBC before each cycle (prolonged neutropenia risk with higher cumulative cyclophosphamide)
renal/bladder toxicity surveillance with cyclophosphamide (mesna as indicated)
coordination of dactinomycin dosing with radiation timing
gonadotoxicity/fertility counseling with cumulative cyclophosphamide exposure

doseModificationRules.condition: poor performance status with Oberlin risk factors greater than 2
doseModificationRules.text: Consider lower/intermediate cumulative cyclophosphamide (8.4 to 16.8 g/m2) regimens and outpatient support per clinical review (footnote d, lines 1764 to 1767).
Hold dactinomycin during overlapping radiation (footnote b, line 1705).

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Pediatric rhabdomyosarcoma VAC per-drug milligram doses are not printed in the provided adult extract (VAC in the adult text refers to M-VAC for bladder cancer, a different regimen), so identity and doses are grounded to the NCCN Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma guideline layer

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma
guideline.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (PRMS-G): very-low/low-risk (lines 1692 to 1699), intermediate-risk VAC backbones (lines 1720 to 1728), high-risk VAC backbones (lines 1748 to 1756); risk-group assignment (lines 600 to 621); FOXO1 molecular markers (Table 1, lines 1133 to 1157; prognostic significance lines 1029 to 1035, 1063 to 1066; FISH line 1109)

provenanceNote: PEDIATRIC ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for rhabdomyosarcoma (StewardMD reference disease rhabdomyosarcoma). Regimen identity is grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma (Rhabdomyosarcoma) v1.2026: VAC = vinCRIStine + Actinomycin-D (Dactinomycin) + Cyclophosphamide per COG ARST0331 (low-risk), ARST0531/D9803 Arm A/ARST2031 (intermediate/high-risk), with the optional alternating VI (vinCRIStine + Irinotecan) block (Principles of Systemic Therapy PRMS-G, lines 1692 to 1767). Risk stratification and the FOXO1 (PAX3/PAX7::FOXO1) fusion biomarker - a stronger outcome predictor than histologic subtype, with alveolar RMS typically fusion-positive and embryonal fusion-negative - are grounded to the Molecular Alterations table (lines 1133 to 1157), fusion-status prognostic significance (lines 1029 to 1035, 1063 to 1066), FISH sufficiency (line 1109), and risk-group assignment (lines 600 to 621). The source prints the cyclophosphamide CUMULATIVE dose by protocol (16.8 g/m2 VAC per ARST0531/ARST2031; 30.8 g/m2 per D9803 Arm A; 8.4 g/m2 when alternating with VI) but does NOT print per-dose milligram values or a fixed cycle length, so every drug basis/dosePerUnit/unit plus cycleLengthDays and cycles are set to the literal VERIFY and listed in verifyFields rather than invented. Pediatric safety scaffolding is retained: cyclophosphamide dose de-intensification (8.4 to 16.8 g/m2) with poor performance and high Oberlin risk factors, mesna as indicated, gonadotoxicity/fertility counseling, and dactinomycin held during overlapping radiation. ISMP tall-man applied (vinCRIStine 2 mg cap). Status is DRAFT with unresolved VERIFY fields. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
